messages:
Owen L.: hi all, Owen here (first day). I ran `kubectl config get-contexts` and only see `minikube`. I need read on `staging` and a personal namespace `onboard-owen` to play with examples. who should I file a ticket with and what exact info do you need? :wave:

Sam (DevEx): welcome Owen! :tada: open an infra ticket and include: corp email, manager, namespaces and perms (read/write), and paste `kubectl config view --minify --flatten`. That helps us merge your kubeconfig.

Owen L.: pasted my flattened kubeconfig (minimal):
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: minikube
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: minikube
```

I created INF-840 and linked my manager @rachel_p.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-840 created and assigned to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-840

Lena (Eng-Infra): hi Owen  we usually create `onboard-<name>` ns and bind `edit` there, and add you to `redwood-staging-read` for staging. I'll provision and post back. If you need temporary staging write, include duration.

Lena (Eng-Infra): done. please verify:
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=onboard-owen
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --namespace=staging
```

Owen L.: verified: contexts show `redwood-staging` and `onboard-owen`, `auth can-i` yes for listing in my ns and no for create in staging (fine). I can create a test pod in my namespace. thanks! :thumbsup:

Sam (DevEx): awesome. tip: to switch namespace quickly: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=onboard-owen`. If kubeconfig gets messy see https://go.redwood/kube-onboard.
